name: atlas
description: Offline-first mapping and navigation platform (OsmAnd-inspired) for Android + Web.

scripts._comment:build:packages: Dependency order is derived from each package's @atlas/* deps by scripts/build-packages.mjs — no hand-maintained wave list. A new package needs no edit here: drop it in packages/, declare its deps, done.
scripts.build: npm run build:packages && npm run build -w @atlas/backend && npm run build -w @atlas/web
scripts.dev: npm run build:packages && concurrently -k -n backend,web -c blue,green "npm:dev:backend" "npm:dev:web"
scripts.typecheck: npm run build:packages && npm run typecheck --workspaces --if-present
scripts._comment:test: Timeouts are raised well above vitest's 5s/10s defaults for one reason: the gate runs inside a docker build on a host that is also serving everything else, and loaded raster tests have reached 55s without a correctness failure — a red build with nothing wrong in it silently leaves the last release undeployed. CPU-heavy potential/backend workspaces also serialize their files so they do not manufacture contention. A hang still fails, just later.
scripts._comment:test:slow: `*.slow.test.ts` is the raster-model tail: five files (backend/src/potential/{hunt,river,lake,derive,health}) that were 16 of the gate's 43 minutes while testing models a typical release never touches. `test` skips them, `test:slow` runs only them, `test:all` runs everything and is what the image build and CI use — the gate that decides a deploy never skips anything. Naming is the whole mechanism: no list to maintain, rename a file to opt in. A slow test gets 300s rather than the fast suite's 90s: the hunt kommune-harvest case measures 73s alone, and 90s left so little headroom that ordinary load on this host (which also serves the deployed stack) timed it out in a release gate with nothing wrong in it -- exactly the red-build-hides-a-good-release failure the note above is about. These tests are minutes long by nature; the timeout is there to catch a hang, not to police their duration.
scripts._comment:gate: The pre-push gate. Runs format/lint/build/typecheck/tests and decides two things from the diff: whether the slow raster tests apply, and whether this change can break the *image* (a package.json, the lockfile, the Dockerfile) and therefore needs the local `docker build` too. CI's image build always runs the full suite regardless.
scripts._comment:parity: The web↔Android parity checklist, read at release time. The gate already enforces it — packages/parity's test resolves every capability's marker in both app trees; this is the human-readable half.
scripts._comment:lint: Both caches live under node_modules/.cache (already ignored everywhere, and dockerignored — the image build re-checks every file from cold, which is the run that counts). Together these two stages were ~5 min of every local gate while re-reading a tree that had not changed; both invalidate on content *and* config change, so a cache hit means the same verdict.
